**Maintainer ruling recorded** — maintainer, 2026-08-17, batch acceptance of the PM decision-inbox recommendations, verbatim: 「同意」. Four-dimension analysis delivered in-session; provenance: PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`.

**Ruled: A, minimal version** — bound `lock_wait_timeout` on the session performing the deferred-DDL widening ALTER, so a blocked `os migrate` fails loudly with an ADR-0112 envelope (closed-vocabulary code, `DATABASE_ERROR` family, naming the lock wait) instead of hanging up to a year. **No retry logic, no configurability** until real demand is measured. Scope: the deferred-DDL flush path; a pin test for the bounded-wait refusal.

The bound's value is the implementer's proposal in the PR (minutes-scale, stated with reasoning), reviewable there. Independent of #9350's held metadata-lock measurement — this makes the failure diagnosable either way.

Label `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #9547. Ready-flip and enqueue **held pending CI convergence** (see the last section).

Reviewer of record: `domain:drivers` seat, round 1, session `session_017qYPmkKEsfbWY1yVg83p8F`. Verified **against GitHub and `origin/main`**, ⛔ not against the report's self-description. Argument lives in the PR; this is the checklist result and the spot readings, ⛔ not a restatement of the PR body.

### Checklist — each read from the API, not the report

| item | reading |
|---|---|
| PR form | draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · first line **`Fixes #9354`** ✅ — correct: this card *should* close on merge, nothing is deferred |
| changed files | **3**, from `get_files`: `sql-driver.ts`, the new `sql-driver-deferred-ddl-lock-wait.test.ts`, `.changeset/deferred-ddl-bounded-lock-wait.md`. Inside the dispatched surface; the changeset is required by the Delivery clause |
| changeset | present, `"@objectstack/driver-sql": patch` ✅ · `Check Changeset` **success** |
| **clause ② — the hard stop I set** | **held.** ⛔ Zero `packages/spec/**` paths in the diff, and `err.code = StandardErrorCode.enum.DATABASE_ERROR` reuses the existing closed vocabulary. Nothing minted ⇒ no fork, no re-dispatch, no `needs:contract-review` |
| governed-path fork | **clean** — no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. Queue-eligible, ⛔ not maintainer-merge |
| refusal-case minimum | met: the pins assert **`code`** (`DATABASE_ERROR`) *and* **`status`** (500), not merely that it threw |
| `content/docs/releases/` | untouched ✅ — the advisory named `releases/v17.mdx` and it was correctly left read-only |

### Spot readings I took myself, because "it's green" is not the same as "the green proved the risk"

⭐ **The dev's most consequential finding is correct, and I verified it independently rather than accepting it.** Its PM-assumption-4 answer claims the file's existing session seam `withUtcSession` is *connection*-level and therefore unusable here. Confirmed on `origin/main`: it installs through `pool.afterCreate` (`sql-driver.ts:4185–4190`). Reusing it would have set `lock_wait_timeout` on **every** connection, bounding unrelated runtime DML — far outside the ruling. Choosing a transaction for connection affinity instead is the right call, and getting this wrong would have been invisible in review.

⚠️ **My own count differs from the report's on one immaterial point, so I state mine:** the report says `knex.transaction` is "already used 6x in this file"; I measure **4** matching lines on `origin/main`. It does not touch the verdict — the seam is established either way — but a count recited in a report is not a measurement, and this seat has paid for that lesson enough times to write down the number it actually took.

⭐ **The `premise_still_valid: true` is load-bearing here and it survived a real second measurement.** The dev re-derived the zero-hit on `lock_wait_timeout` with the same positive control I used, independently — so the "nothing bounds this today" premise has now been established twice, by two parties, with a control both times.

### The material finding beyond the dispatch — credited

The dispatch told it to bound the wait. It found that **bounding alone would not have satisfied the ruling**: `migrateMysqlDatetimeColumns` catches, warns and returns, so a bounded MySQL error was being discarded — `os migrate apply` would have printed "Applied 0 change(s)" and exited **0**, converting a year-long hang into a *silent no-op reporting success*. That is a worse failure than the one being fixed, and neither the card, the ruling, nor my dispatch order named it.

Its response is correctly scoped: **one** condition escapes the swallow (errno 1205 / `ER_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, followed through `cause`), only while the flush flag is set, with boot-sync deliberately left unbounded and swallowing and **pinned as such**. ⭐ Refusing to sniff message text — because MySQL and MariaDB word and translate it differently — is the correct instinct: a prose recognizer fails silently in another locale, straight back to the year-long hang.

**Reverse verification accepted as real**: two ablations, direction predicted *before* running, both landing where predicted (6 red/4 green; 3 red/7 green — exactly the three bound pins). ⭐ Ablation A going red also settles the stale-`dist` question by demonstration rather than assertion — a stale read would have stayed green.

### Deviations — all declared, none silent, none requiring rework

1. **Scope widened to both widening ALTERs** (datetime + time twin) rather than the datetime one alone. This is exactly the "defensible if they share the seam" case my dispatch flagged, and they share it literally. Bounding one while its twin waits a year would leave `os migrate` hanging with the operator unable to tell which ALTER hung. **Accepted.** Create-table/add-column DDL correctly left unbounded as materially larger than the ruled scope.
2. **File-surface breach declined rather than taken** — `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx` matched by subject and was *not* edited, because `content/docs/**` was outside the dispatched surface. Filed as **#9543** instead. ⭐ This is the right reflex and the opposite of the usual failure; the surface line held under a real temptation to cross it.
3. **The bound's value (120s) is argued, not asserted** — the ruling delegated it and the reasoning is genuinely decision-shaped (above OLTP noise by ~3 orders of magnitude; below operator patience; asymmetric cost since the widening is idempotent and re-runnable). Reviewable in the PR, which is where the ruling put it.

### Two residual limits — recorded, ⛔ not rework, and not to be quoted as covered

1. ⚠️ **`withPinnedSession` is overridden in the pins, so the real `knex.transaction` seam is not exercised by them.** The session-identity assertion proves the *fake's* counter matches — it proves the seam's shape, not that knex hands both statements one connection. The dev states this plainly rather than dressing it up. Structurally sound and the correct trade (faking less would need a live MySQL), but "both statements provably ride one session" is proven **by construction**, not by the suite. `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is the job that could contradict it and is being watched.
2. ⚠️ **The restore is best-effort in a way that can leak the bound.** If the `select @@session.lock_wait_timeout` probe fails, `prior` is undefined and the `finally` skips the restore, so the connection returns to the pool carrying 120s. Low severity and the leak points the *safe* way (a 120s bound on later work rather than a year), which is why this is a note and not a REWORK.

### Filing hygiene — one gap, triage-visible, ⛔ not corrected by me

- **#9543** ✅ unassigned, `finding`, correctly anchored.
- **#9542** — well-formed and unassigned, but carries **no labels at all**. Not silently fixed here: a fully bare card is precisely disjunct ① of triage's own sweep, so it *will* be picked up; labelling it myself would be an execution seat producing a routing signal. Named in the round report instead.

### ⛔ Why this is not enqueued yet

At review time CI reads **9 success · 2 skipped · 11 `in_progress` · 0 red** — including `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Test Core (1–3/3)`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check`. `in_progress` is an honest reading, not a green: **gate convergence is the review side's obligation and the ready-flip waits on every job's OWN conclusion.**

⭐ Per this seat's standing commitment, **arming the flip-point check is part of this ACCEPT, not a follow-up to it** — a re-read is armed for 09:23Z. A reviewed-ACCEPT PR still sitting in draft is a state this seat names out loud, because 「waiting」 and 「forgotten」 look identical on GitHub.

The dev's report recorded `typecheck => tsc --noEmit exit 0`. Read from `origin/main`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/tsconfig.json` carries `"include": ["src/**/*"]` with no `*.test.ts` exclusion — and the new pin file was added at **`src/sql-driver-deferred-ddl-lock-wait.test.ts`**, inside `src/`. So the package typecheck **does** compile the new test, and CI is reading a surface the dev's run reported clean. Establishing which of the two runs was wrong is part of the patch round.

⭐ Live instance of a standing lesson: **a dev's local gate exit code is not a fact about CI**, in either direction.

### Bounds carried into the patch round, unchanged

⛔ Not fixable by excluding the test from tsconfig, by `as any`, by raising any ledger (baselines may only shrink), or by moving the file out of `src/` — if the honest fix needs a tsconfig change that is a **fork**, to be reported, not taken quietly. The clause-② hard stop still stands. The 120s bound, the both-ALTERs scope and the swallow-escape design were reviewed and accepted and are ⛔ not reopened.

⚠️ **A patch commit resets the whole gate farm** — `0c9a3db`'s 9 greens do not carry forward, and the re-read starts from zero on the new head.
